title: 202 followed by 429 while a Flow action is still running is shown as a step failure
text: Hi, We have a custom Flow action that sometimes cannot finish inside Flow’s 10-second response window. We followed the action endpoint contract in Create Flow action endpoints , and the same pattern was discussed in Retry-After is ignored in flow action response . The action is running normally, but the workflow run UI presents it as a failure: and in run details: On our side all is implemented according to the documentation, but because of how UI communicates the in-progress workflow action, merchants are sometimes frustrated and attempt to retry the workflow from the Flow manually. What we return for one action_run_id : The first POST returns 202 with an empty body, in well under a second. The work is accepted and continues asynchronously. We do not return 200 until the action has actually been fully finished. Later POSTs for the same action_run_id , while the work is still in progress, return 429 with Retry-After (seconds, between 5 and 3600) and a short body that tells that this action is still in progress. When the work is finished we return 200 with an empty body, or 400 with a merchant-facing message if it permanently failed (e.g. provided payload is incorrect or action was a duplicate, etc). That matches the documented meanings: 202: accepted, not yet processed. Flow resends the POST at increasing intervals for up to 36 hours. 429 with Retry-After : minimum wait of 5–3600 seconds, plus jitter, with longer waits after repeated 429s. 200: processed. Any other 4xx: failed, and the merchant should see that response. What the merchant sees While step 2 is still returning 429, the run shows: “This step has errors” “This action failed and we’re retrying it. Check step configuration.” Nothing is misconfigured, and the action has not failed. Flow is correctly retrying an in-progress action. The copy tells the merchant the opposite. We also tried answering every poll with 202. The endpoint still answered in a few hundred milliseconds, but Flow then recorded: Ran into transient error: Waited over 10 seconds for non-202 response with the step status Retrying. From the logs, that 10 seconds is Flow waiting after a fast 202 for a non-202 status. It is not our server taking 10 seconds to respond. Returning 429 on the later polls is what produces that non-202 status, which is why we do it. Flow then displays the 429 as an error anyway. Shop we used for testing: rate-limit-test.myshopify.com Sample action_run_id : bf869cdc49a0b2e381826690d54e84e9302d8f08 Time shown in Flow: Oct 14, 2026 at 8:56 PM (store timezone) We double checked logs to ensure that the endpoint is answering inside the 10-second limit. Our request / suggestion: Please treat 202, and 429 with Retry-After, as “still running” until the run ends with 200 or a non-retryable 4xx, or until the 36-hour retry window is exhausted. While those retries are in progress the status may be something like: “This action is still running.”. From our point of view, when Flow UI says that the action failed, or to check the step configuration, this provides negative UX for both merchant and us. A real failure should stay reserved for a non-429 4xx, or for retries that stop after 36 hours. Happy to provide a workflow run link or more logs. 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Custom Flow action timing out and incorrectly showing as step failure.

title: Feature request: SEPA Direct Debit for subscriptions, with iDEAL/Bancontact as the first payment
text: Feature request: SEPA Direct Debit for subscriptions, with iDEAL/Bancontact as the first payment Please add native support in Shopify Payments for the following subscription flow: The customer pays initially through iDEAL or Bancontact. During checkout, the customer authorizes a SEPA Direct Debit mandate. Subsequent subscription payments are collected automatically through SEPA Direct Debit. This is a familiar subscription experience in the Netherlands and Belgium, where customers commonly use bank payments rather than credit cards. Stripe already supports using iDEAL and Bancontact to establish SEPA Direct Debit payment details for future payments. Since Shopify Payments uses Stripe as a payment processing partner, it would be valuable to expose this capability for Shopify subscriptions as well. I understand that iDEAL and Bancontact themselves are one-time payment methods. The request is to use them for the initial payment and mandate setup, with SEPA Direct Debit handling renewals. Currently, merchants need additional integrations to offer this flow, adding cost and complexity. Native support would let European customers subscribe using their preferred payment method while keeping checkout and subscription management within Shopify. Is this on the Shopify Payments roadmap? 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant requesting native subscription payment flow for SEPA and iDEAL.

title: Shopify Payments Is Fully Set Up, but I Still Can't Connect My Bank Account — Almost 2 Weeks Without a Solution
text: I’m posting this because I’m extremely frustrated with how Shopify has handled an issue that has prevented me from starting my business for almost two weeks. I recently opened my Shopify store and completed the Shopify Payments setup process. A Shopify support agent confirmed that my Shopify Payments account was fully set up and verified. However, whenever I try to connect my bank account, the connection is declined, and I’m unable to proceed. After contacting Shopify Support multiple times, I was eventually informed that PayPal is one of the third-party partner that Shopify Payments work with and they are responsible for this bank account connection decline. However, nobody has been able to explain the actual reason for the decline or provide a solution. The most frustrating part is that I’m being told to wait for PayPal to respond to Shopify’s email. It has now been almost two weeks, and I’m still waiting for an explanation from PayPal. Despite repeatedly asking Shopify Support to escalate the issue through direct escalation channels rather than simply waiting for an email response, I continue to receive vague updates that the team is still investigating the root cause. I’ve had to contact multiple support agents and repeatedly push for an escalation just to get someone to follow up on the issue. Even after the case was flagged as urgent, I still haven’t received a concrete answer or a clear timeline for resolution. Let me make one thing clear: I signed up for Shopify Payments, not PayPal. I’m using Shopify’s service, and this is a problem with the payment setup process that Shopify provides to its merchants. I understand that Shopify works with third-party partners behind the scenes. However, that shouldn’t mean merchants are left waiting indefinitely with no explanation, no actionable solution, and no clear timeline simply because a third-party partner hasn’t responded. I have only just opened my store and haven’t even had the chance to start selling. I’ve done nothing wrong, yet I’m losing valuable time while paying for a service that I cannot fully use. I don’t want to use another third-party payment processor. I specifically want to use Shopify Payments, and I expect Shopify to take ownership of this issue and help resolve it. Here is what I’m asking Shopify to do: Escalate this issue through direct channels with PayPal instead of continuing to wait for an email response. Provide a clear explanation of why my bank account connection is being declined , rather than repeatedly telling me that the team is still investigating. Involve the appropriate payment leadership team and explain what alternative solution Shopify can offer if PayPal fails to respond or takes too long to respond. Provide a concrete action plan and timeline for resolution , rather than leaving me in the dark indefinitely. I chose Shopify because I expected a reliable platform that would help me launch and operate my business. Instead, almost two weeks have passed without a resolution, and I still cannot properly get started. Has anyone else experienced this issue recently? Were you eventually able to connect your bank account, and how long did it take to resolve? I would also appreciate an official response from Shopify explaining what merchants are supposed to do when a third-party partner blocks their bank account connection and provides no timely resolution. Merchants shouldn’t have to spend weeks chasing support just to get a basic payment setup issue resolved. 4 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
triage_reason: Merchant blocked from starting business due to bank connection failure.
